perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s perspective, I have access to the following:

- I am Bradley Ochoa, a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague and the marketing manager. Our working relationship feels professional but sometimes strained over sales versus marketing strategy.
- I prepared data and charts from our last five campaigns to support my belief that traditional sales techniques are being overlooked in favor of newer digital marketing strategies Katherine has been implementing.
- In our meeting, I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed traditional methods could better help core sales. She said the market is evolving, that we cannot ignore digital outreach, and asked how I reconcile my data with increasing online engagement. I replied that I did not want to abandon digital marketing, but I felt proven methods were being sidelined without proper consideration. She said she understood, that it is about balance, and suggested analyzing the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories that significantly boosted engagement and sales. I found the results impressive and began to question my support for only traditional methods. I asked her to explain how those strategies are developed. She said it is about targeting the right audience with the right message and offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making behind a recent campaign. I admitted my doubts and said seeing the outcomes made me want to understand the digital approach. She was glad I was open and said adapting to market trends is important.
- I then proposed a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital approaches. Katherine agreed, saying combining our strengths could lead to better results, and we planned to schedule time to brainstorm and outline next steps. I said I was hopeful about leveraging both our expertise and appreciated her willingness to collaborate. She said she looked forward to leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After our joint meeting, I felt excited and worked overtime to prepare a board presentation draft integrating both our ideas. I told Katherine about it. She reviewed it, praised it as comprehensive and well thought out, and noted my hard work. I said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart from competitors and wanted to nail the presentation. She expressed confidence and suggested going through it once more to fine-tune it.
- After our presentation was successful and the new strategy was implemented, I felt grateful for my professional growth and our collaboration. I thanked Katherine and proposed regular strategy sessions. She said it was a pleasure seeing the project succeed, credited my openness to new ideas, and agreed that regular sessions would help us stay on top of our game and market trends.

I do not have access to Katherine’s private thoughts, hidden motivations, or any narrator-only facts about her beyond what she said or did in these interactions.
